name: command-line-usage-markup-syntax-cliss
behavioral_change: In command-line-usage v_new (5.0.0), inline ansi formatting inside section content switched from the ansi-escape-sequences markup `[style]{text}` to chalk template literal syntax `{style text}`. The function signatures and exports are unchanged; only the interpretation of the string content changed, so an old-style string such as `[red]{Required}` now makes chalk throw `Found extraneous } in Chalk template literal`.
downstream_effect: cliss builds `[red]{Required}` and `[underline]{<type>}` strings in `prepareOptions` in lib/cli-help.js, so every help-rendering path in the child-process CLI throws after the upgrade and the mocha tests see `Command failed` with the child's stderr. All stack frames fall inside node_modules (chalk and command-line-usage internals); lib/cli-help.js is never named, and the error text does not say which downstream string is at fault or that the markup syntax changed.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes two lines in `prepareOptions` in lib/cli-help.js, replacing `[red]{Required}` with `{red Required}` and `[underline]{${option.type}}` with `{underline ${option.type}}`.
documented_in: The command-line-usage v5.0.0 release notes announce that all inline ansi formatting is now handled by chalk template literal syntax and, in the Upgrading section, show the code form `{underline some text}` (mis-recording the old form as `[underline](some text)`). The README examples for `typeLabel` also change from `'[underline]{file}'` in 4.1.0 to `'{underline file}'` in 5.0.5, showing the new code form.
